name: Rockfish tacos with pomegranate and lime yogurt
yield: Dinner for one, about six tacos
intro: Mild local rockfish seared hard and flaked into warm tortillas with peppery arugula, cold lime yogurt, and pomegranate that bursts like salsa.

steps.text: Salt the fish and leave it on a plate. Pat it completely dry right before it goes in the pan.
Stir the zest of the lime, half its juice, and a pinch of salt into the yogurt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until they blister in spots. Stack them under a towel.

Heat a nonstick or well-seasoned carbon-steel or cast-iron skillet over medium-high with a thin film of oil until it shimmers — rockfish is delicate and sticks to anything else. Lay the fish in, away from you, and don't touch it until it lets go of the pan on its own.
Flip and cook until it's opaque all the way through and flakes easily, then flake it in the pan with a fork.
Two tortillas, fish, arugula, a spoonful of lime yogurt, pomegranate on top, the rest of the lime squeezed over.

how_it_works: A mild fish tastes of very little on its own, so everything around it is sharp, cold, or peppery: lime, yogurt, pomegranate, arugula. The sear is the technique — dry fish, hot pan, hands off — and it works on any firm fillet.
swaps: Any firm white fish — cod or halibut — works the same way.
For heat, warm olive oil with garlic and chile flakes and spoon it over instead of the yogurt.
Smear ajvar on the tortillas first for smoke.
leftovers: Leftover fish is good cold the next day, on toast with lemon and olive oil.

sources.title: Fish Tacos on the Grill — Food52
sources.note: 2–4 minutes a side for thin white fillets, in a pan if you have no grill
